subject: Stratacorp pricing parity request — interoperability and pilot path
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratacorp.com
Date: 2026-08-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing parity ask + quick tech notes

Marissa,

We spoke briefly with our engineering and procurement teams this morning. StrataCorp is evaluating a vendor swap and we need a formal price parity offer to compare against our current supplier. Key points:

- Target: match their effective unit cost over a 12‑month run-rate (details attached: Strata_TCO_v2.xlsx).
- We need clarity on dedicated capacity pricing (SLA-backed) and any migration credits.
- Ops compatibility: our stack relies heavily on persistent KV cache and 1,024 token avg sequences — any quantization/compatibility caveats?

Can you send options (credits vs committed discount vs pilot credit) and a crisp mutual action plan? Procurement would like this by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Daniel
Procurement Lead
StrataCorp

Attachment: Strata_TCO_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratacorp.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + quick tech notes

Daniel — thanks for the clear ask and the TCO. High level response and three options we can move quickly on:

1) Short pilot: 6‑week pilot with $25k onboarding credit + technical migration support (includes KV cache export+import workshop). No long‑term commit.
2) Committed run: 12‑month committed capacity at a stepped discount (starts at 15% off list, moves to 22% at >1.2M tokens/month) plus a one‑time migration credit that offsets onboarding costs.
3) Hybrid: 3‑month pilot credit + option to convert to committed run with a prorated buyout.

Important technical note (from infra): some older model quantizations used by the competitor are incompatible with our smallest-CPU fallbacks; we can guarantee parity on quality for the recommended quantization profile but KV cache migration will require a short compatibility shim (we'll handle it in the pilot).

I've drafted a short term sheet and MAP (mutual action plan) — attaching a concise term sheet and linking a playbook we use. If StrataCorp wants SLA-backed dedicated pools, we'll price that separately and include an SLA addendum.

Next steps: call with procurement + Eng to confirm which option you prefer; we can have the term sheet updated within 24 hours.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-strata-term-sheet-draft.pdf (term sheet stub)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cExampleDoc

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + quick tech notes — infra details

Daniel / Marissa,

Quick note from infra/serving runtime side on compatibility and risk mitigation:

- Sequence length: 1,024 tokens is within our sweet spot. Latency delta vs competitor depends on batching profile; for interactive SLAs we'll reserve smaller batch windows to keep P95 predictable.
- KV cache: we can export the cache from your current runtime (standard JSON+binary blobs) and import into our runtime; the only migration nontriviality is if your current provider uses a proprietary compressed KV format — in that case we supply a conversion script as part of the pilot.
- Quantization: recommend we use our 4‑bit quant profile for cost parity while preserving model quality; we'll run a quick eval on your prompt set during the pilot.

I've added a brief playbook section to the shared Drive doc with steps and estimated timelines.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Eng
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cExampleDoc

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratacorp.com, legal@stratacorp.com
Date: 2026-08-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + quick tech notes

Thanks, Marissa and Jonas — this is helpful.

A few asks before we move to a term sheet:

- SOC 2 evidence and SSO/SAML integration details (our security team needs to validate).
- Dedicated capacity SLA: if you include a 99.9% uptime commitment and credits for missed SLOs, we can prioritize conversion to committed run.
- Pilot cap: we prefer a $30k cost cap for the pilot; your $25k onboarding credit would be acceptable if compute overage is guaranteed to be under $5k.

Can we schedule a 30‑minute exec/tech sync next Tuesday? Procurement + Eng + Security will join.

Regards,
Daniel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + quick tech notes — term sheet and next steps

Daniel,

Appended is our commercial term sheet (redwood-strata-term-sheet-aug26.pdf) with three pricing options mapped to the scenarios Marissa outlined. Highlights:

- Option A (pilot): $0 onboarding fee after $25k credit; compute capped at $30k; SLA not included.
- Option B (committed): 18% effective discount at 1.0M tokens/month commit, includes one‑time $75k migration credit and 99.9% SLA with service credits.
- Option C (hybrid): 3‑month pilot convertible to committed run with pro‑rated migration credit.

Next steps: confirm preferred option and we'll circulate an MSA + SLA addendum for legal review. I've linked the HubSpot deal and included the draft term sheet in attachments.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-strata-term-sheet-aug26.pdf (term sheet, pricing table)
